settings.label: Conversation Sharing
settings.description: Generate a link that lets any Googler load a read-only copy of a conversation. Sharing exports the conversation history to your public x20 folder, so it needs that folder to be readable by others.

settings.label: Inline Actions
settings.description: Show a floating notification card when background conversations need your input. Answer questions, approve commands, and grant permissions without leaving your current conversation. Share feedback at go/inline-actions-feedback.

settings.label: Always Proceed
settings.description: Agent never asks for review. This maximizes the autonomy of the Agent, but also has the highest risk of the Agent operating over unsafe or injected Artifact content.

settings.label: Always Ask
settings.description: Agent always asks for review.

settings.label: Allow List Terminal Commands
settings.description: The agent auto-executes commands matched by an allow list entry.

settings.label: Deny List Terminal Commands
settings.description: The agent asks for permission before executing commands matched by a deny list entry.

settings.label: Agent Auto-Fix Lints
settings.description: Give the agent awareness of lint errors created by its edits so it can fix them without explicit prompting.

settings.label: Queued Messages
settings.description: Configure when follow-up messages are sent.

settings.label: Strict Mode
settings.description: Enforce settings that prevent the agent from autonomously running targeted exploits and require human review for all agent actions. Visit antigravity.google/docs/strict-mode for details.

settings.label: Agent Non-Workspace File Access
settings.description: Allow the agent to automatically view and edit files outside the current workspace. Use with caution: this gives the agent access to additional potentially-relevant information, but also allows the agent to access credential files, secrets, and other files outside of the workspace that could be targeted in prompt injection attacks or other exploits by malicious actors.

settings.label: Command Setup Script
settings.description: A shell setup script run before every command the agent executes.

settings.label: Enable Terminal Sandbox
settings.description: Run terminal commands with sandbox restrictions.

settings.label: Sandbox Allow Network
settings.description: Allow sandboxed commands to make network requests.

settings.label: Enable Shell Integration
settings.description: Use the IDE's shell integration to detect and report terminal command execution. When disabled, the agent uses its own shell. Restart the application for this to take effect.

settings.label: Review Policy
settings.description: Specifies the agent's behavior when asking for review on artifacts, which are documents it creates to enable a richer conversation experience.

settings.label: Enable Sounds for Agent
settings.description: Play a sound when the agent finishes generating a response.

settings.label: Enable Notifications for Agent
settings.description: Show browser notifications when your action is needed or execution finishes.

settings.label: Auto-Expand Changes Overview
settings.description: Automatically expand the Changes Overview toolbar when the agent finishes generating a response.

settings.label: [Dev] GCP Project ID
settings.description: GCP Project ID for enterprise features.

settings.label: Conversation History
settings.description: Let the agent access past conversations to inform its responses.

settings.label: Knowledge
settings.description: Let the agent access its knowledge base to inform its responses and automatically generate knowledge items in the background. Turning this off prevents the agent from accessing existing knowledge items, but doesn't delete them.

settings.label: Auto-Open Edited Files
settings.description: Open files in the background if the agent creates or edits them

settings.label: Open Agent on Reload
settings.description: Open the agent panel on window reload

settings.label: Verbose Agent Chat
settings.description: Display and preserve intermediate thinking steps.

settings.label: Conversation Width
settings.description: Configure the maximum width of the conversation panel.

settings.label: Markdown Artifact Width
settings.description: Configure the default width of markdown artifacts.

settings.label: Table Width
settings.description: Configure the default width of tables.

settings.label: Suggestions in Editor
settings.description: Show suggestions when typing in the editor

settings.label: Tab to Jump
settings.description: Predict the location of your next edit and navigate you there with a tab keypress.

settings.label: Tab to Import
settings.description: Quickly add and update imports with a tab keypress.

settings.label: Tab Speed
settings.description: Set the speed of tab suggestions

settings.label: Highlight After Accept
settings.description: Highlight newly inserted text after accepting a Tab completion.

settings.label: Tab Gitignore Access
settings.description: Allow Tab to view and edit the files in .gitignore. Use with caution if your .gitignore lists files containing credentials, secrets, or other sensitive information.

settings.label: Enable Browser Tools
settings.description: Let the agent use browser tools to open URLs, read web pages, and interact with browser content. This gives the agent access to important (and often critical) knowledge and methods of validation, but any browser integration does increase exposure to external malicious parties for security exploits.

settings.label: Browser Javascript Execution Policy
settings.description: Controls whether the agent can run custom JavaScript to automate complex browser actions.

settings.label: Chrome Binary Path
settings.description: Path to the Chrome/Chromium executable. Leave empty for auto-detection.

settings.label: Browser User Profile Path
settings.description: Custom path for the browser user profile directory. Leave empty for default (~/.gemini/antigravity-browser-profile).

settings.label: Browser CDP Port
settings.description: Port number for Chrome DevTools Protocol remote debugging. Leave empty for default (9222).

settings.label: Include Jetski Default Customizations
settings.description: Include default customizations, such as default skills.

settings.label: Prevent Sleep
settings.description: Prevent the computer from sleeping while the app is running.

settings.label: Keep In Menu Bar
settings.description: Keep the app accessible from the menu bar and running in the background when all windows are closed.

settings.label: Automatic Check for Updates
settings.description: Automatically prompt you to restart the app when a new update is available. When disabled, you can check for updates manually from the app menu.

settings.label: Enable Remote Control
settings.description: Manage your conversations from the companion website.

settings.label: Nickname
settings.description: A nickname for identifying this application in the companion website. Changing this will restart the connection.

settings.label: Conversation Sharing
settings.description: Generate a link that lets any Googler load a read-only copy of a conversation. Sharing exports the conversation history to your public x20 folder, so it needs that folder to be readable by others.

settings.label: Inline Actions
settings.description: Show a floating notification card when background conversations need your input. Answer questions, approve commands, and grant permissions without leaving your current conversation. Share feedback at go/inline-actions-feedback.

settings.label: CitC Workspace VCS
settings.description: VCS used when creating a new CitC workspace, including workspaces generated based off your initial prompt.

settings.label: Use full VCS clones for Best of N
settings.description: Give each Best of N fork a full clone of your workspace, including its local commit history (Fig and Piper only; JJ temporarily falls back to standard CitC clones). Choosing a winner then gives your workspace that fork's state, so the commits it made are kept. Forks take longer to create than the default CitC clone. See go/jetski-best-of-n.

settings.label: Use full Git clones for Best of N
settings.description: Give each Best of N fork its own clone of your Git repository instead of a copy-on-write overlay. Each fork is then a real repository, so commits it makes are kept when you choose it as the winner. Forks take longer to create, and the wait grows with the size of your repository. See go/jetski-best-of-n.
